findings: All nine total-latency comparisons have matching primary and mean-sensitivity directions; fixed/adaptive has no all-six-pairs latency winner in any fixture.
Early cold-hot is a no-resize control: both enabled modes have the same calls, hits, collisions and capacity. Its latency difference cannot be attributed to eliminated rehashes.
Late cold-hot preserves reuse and removes four resizes: lower tail allocation and metadata reservation do not produce a consistent tail CPU or end-to-end latency improvement.
Warm-cycle-8192 exposes the capacity cost: fixed causes 3.305779033348 times the lazy source calls, higher tail allocation and higher tail CPU, although paired total latency is near one.
Cross-JVM allocation differences are concentrated before the prefix, with largely stable within-JVM allocations. These descriptive clusters do not establish a JIT, GC or growth cause.
Paired ratios need not agree with a ratio of marginal arm medians; neither those marginal ratios nor the mean sensitivity replace the prespecified primary estimator.
CPU and allocation sums hold per query; separately aggregated medians need not add to the median total.

scope.allocation: All-thread allocation retains the older, wider interval through capture.close in finally. Caller allocation ends before that finally. Their difference is not a pure background-thread allocation measurement.
scope.cpu: Current query thread only. GC, JIT and other worker CPU are excluded; counter-read boundaries are adjacent to, but not simultaneous with, elapsed-time snapshots.
scope.gc: Natural G1 events over each whole JVM, including setup and warmups. Concurrent durations overlap. Ordered rows retain Values, so these results do not establish useful-key GC rematerialization.
scope.memory: Global process-authority accounting during serial query windows; no separate query-ledger peak or total retained-heap estimate. Metadata reservations are checked including resize overlap.
scope.phase: Caller CPU and allocation differences reconcile exactly at shared counter snapshots. To-prefix includes connection, preparation, evaluation and prefix consumption. Tail ends after the final exhaustion check, before explicit result/connection close; any cleanup triggered by exhaustion is included. After-consume includes explicit close and retained reads. This cohort fully consumes results and retains no consumer rows.
scope.sourceCalls: Lazy source calls are not physical decodes. Cleared occupied-slot observations precede key comparison; occupied wrappers at close are not a live-Value census. No cross-process ID equality assumed.
scope.statistics: Six same-round ratios of five-query JVM medians. Mean sensitivity is prespecified and separate. Diagnostics do not replace the primary estimator.
